data.title: Hydroxyurea (hydroxycarbamide)
data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Immunomodulators_

**Class:** Antimetabolite; ribonucleotide reductase inhibitor

## Mechanism of action
- Inhibits ribonucleotide reductase → no deoxyribonucleotides → blocks DNA synthesis (S-phase)
- Antiproliferative for keratinocytes; raises fetal haemoglobin (sickle cell)

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Psoriasis (refractory; older alternative to methotrexate), HIV (historical with didanosine)
- Hypereosinophilic syndrome, myeloproliferative disorders (polycythaemia vera, CML, essential thrombocythaemia), sickle cell disease

## Dose & formulations
- Psoriasis: 500 mg–1.5 g/day (1–2 g in divided doses), adjusted to blood counts

## Adverse effects
- Bone marrow suppression (megaloblastic anaemia, leucopenia); macrocytosis is expected
- Skin: painful leg ulcers (malleolar), dermatomyositis-like eruption (hands — 'hydroxyurea dermopathy'), xerosis, hyperpigmentation (skin, nails — longitudinal melanonychia), lichenoid eruptions, alopecia
- Squamous cell carcinoma and actinic keratoses with long-term use (photo-exposed sites)
- GI upset, fever, hepatitis

## Contraindications
- Marked marrow suppression, pregnancy, breastfeeding

## Drug interactions
- Other myelosuppressants; didanosine/stavudine (pancreatitis, neuropathy)

## Monitoring
- CBC every 1–2 weeks initially, then monthly; LFT, renal function; skin examination

## Pregnancy & lactation
Contraindicated (teratogenic).

## Viva points
- Ribonucleotide reductase inhibitor
- Leg ulcers and dermatomyositis-like eruption
- Melanonychia and SCC with long-term use

_Sources: Wolverton 4e ch.19 (Cytotoxic agents); Khopkar (Non-steroidal immunosuppressive drugs). Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
